description: The pie chart, titled “6 Matches,” visually represents the distribution of outcomes across seven categories, labeled 0 through 6, likely corresponding to the number of matches in a dataset or experiment. The largest segment, labeled “6 Matches,” occupies 27.2% of the chart (8006 instances) and is colored in a medium blue. The second-largest segment, “2 Matches,” accounts for 22.4% (6583 instances) and is shown in light green. The “1 Match” category represents 13.8% (4046 instances) in pale yellow, while “0 Matches” makes up 13.3% (3910 instances) in off-white. Smaller segments include “5 Matches” at 10.4% (3043 instances, light blue), “3 Matches” at 6.8% (2002 instances, olive green), and “4 Matches” at 6.2% (1810 instances, slightly darker light blue). Each slice is clearly labeled with its percentage and absolute count, and the segments are arranged in descending order clockwise from the top. The chart uses distinct pastel colors for each category and does not include a separate legend, as labels are placed directly on or adjacent to the slices. This visualization appears to be part of the “Fair-PP” paper, which focuses on aligning large language models with personalized preferences related to social equity, suggesting this chart may illustrate match frequency in a preference alignment task.
